Gala Chongguang, the younger brother of ハン Gangji. 　　Inscriptions: "Seal of Gala Chongguang", "Seonghuang Essence House" and "Jiang Shang Wai Shi". The first seal is "Master Hua Yi". The seal of the collection is "Collection of Yangchen". 　　The "Five-Rhyme Poem" scroll is a five-verse poem written by Gala Chongguang to Ran Qu. Ran Qu is Wu Zhan, character Boqi, number Ran Qu, Suiyang (now Shangqiu County, Henan Province), Qing Dynasty literati, Qing Shunzhi 15 years (1658) scholar, once in Gala Chongguang's hometown Zhenjiang official, Tang Bin for him to write "Jiangnan Zhenjiang Prefecture sea defense co-governor Ran Qu Wu Gong epitaph". Wang Wenzhi, a famous calligrapher from Gala Chongguang's hometown, commented on Gala Chongguang's calligraphy in his book "Inscriptions on the Hall of Quick Rain": "He was a master of all kinds of calligraphy, from chapter and cursive to Su and Mi. The calligrapher's style is superb, with an aura of overwhelming clouds." It can be said to be highly esteemed. Gala Chongguang lived at a time when the calligraphic style of Dong Qichang was most prevalent, and it was fashionable for the entire court and the public to revere Dong. In his book "Shu Raft", he wrote: "The horizontal painting of the hair (starting stroke) is up, the vertical painting of the hair stroke is down, the hair stroke of the skew is heavy, and the hair stroke of the down is light. ......" This work, with its rounded dots and lines, and its natural movement, is based on Mi Fu's example, and the brush is used with confidence. It is full of calm, leisurely and elegant rhythm between the lines.
